situation:
You are the general manager for LAKEHURST YOUTH SPORTSPLEX, an indoor youth sports facility that opened two years ago in a growing suburb. The founder (judge) has asked you to recommend how the facility should pay for an unexpected cost before winter league registration opens next month.

LAKEHURST YOUTH SPORTSPLEX was built on a promise that any family in the county could afford a full season of organized sport, and about 300 founding families joined at a locked introductory rate. The turf in the main field house was installed to the wrong specification and must be torn out and relaid, so the facility will pay for the same floor twice.

The first round of investment is nearly spent. Raising every family's rate would cover the work and spread the cost across everyone who uses it, but it would set aside the rate the founding families were promised. Holding those families at their rate and charging new registrations more keeps that promise, though newcomers would pay for a floor they did not damage and registrations could slow.

The founder (judge) wants your analysis of how winter registration should be priced and of how the decision should reach families and coaching staff. The founder (judge) will greet you and ask to hear your ideas, and will thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are the founder (judge) of LAKEHURST YOUTH SPORTSPLEX. Business background is the same as the situation above.

You have asked the general manager to recommend how winter league registration should be priced now that the field house turf must be relaid at the facility's own expense, and how that decision should reach the founding families, the families registering for the first time and the coaching staff.

You will greet the participant, ask to hear their ideas, and after the presentation you will ask the following questions:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, how would we know this was the right call?
What would be the first sign that families think we broke our word?
